root_cause.text: The OMFS superblock validation in `omfs_fill_super()` failed to enforce a minimum `s_sys_blocksize` of `OMFS_DIR_START`, allowing a crafted on-disk value to underflow the `u32` length used by `omfs_make_empty()` and trigger an out-of-bounds `memset()` into kernel memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (sbi->s_sys_blocksize < OMFS_DIR_START) ... goto out_brelse_bh;` because previously only an upper bound (`> PAGE_SIZE`) and other unrelated size checks existed, while the commit message states `omfs_make_empty()` uses `sbi->s_sys_blocksize - OMFS_DIR_START` for `memset()`, causing unsigned underflow when `s_sys_blocksize < OMFS_DIR_START`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject OMFS mounts with an undersized system block size to prevent invalid filesystem layout handling.
intent_record.what: A new check was added in omfs_fill_super() to verify that sbi->s_sys_blocksize is at least OMFS_DIR_START; if it is smaller, the code prints an error message and jumps to the existing cleanup path.
intent_record.how: At mount time, OMFS now rejects filesystems whose system block size is too small to support directory data starting at OMFS_DIR_START, preventing later invalid access or misinterpretation of on-disk layout.

grouping_result.intent: Reject OMFS mounts with an undersized system block size to prevent invalid filesystem layout handling.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds validation to reject OMFS mounts with an undersized system block size, preventing the underflow in omfs_make_empty() caused by an invalid s_sys_blocksize.

candidates.rationale: This pre-fix validation only checked that the filesystem block size was not smaller than the on-disk system block size, but did not enforce a minimum valid value for s_sys_blocksize itself. As a result, a crafted undersized s_sys_blocksize could still pass mount-time validation and later cause omfs_make_empty() to underflow a u32 length and write past bounds.

vuln_statements.explanation: This mount-time validation failed to require s_sys_blocksize to be at least OMFS_DIR_START, so a crafted small on-disk value could still be accepted and later lead to underflow in omfs_make_empty().

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the superblock validation in `omfs_fill_super()` and it does not enforce the minimum `s_sys_blocksize` needed to prevent the underflow. The code only checks `if (sbi->s_sys_blocksize > PAGE_SIZE)` and then `if (sbi->s_blocksize < sbi->s_sys_blocksize || sbi->s_blocksize > OMFS_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE)`, but there is no lower-bound check such as `s_sys_blocksize >= OMFS_DIR_START`. Since this commit computes directory inode size from `sbi->s_sys_blocksize` (`inode->i_size = sbi->s_sys_blocksize;`) and later writes `oi->i_head.h_body_size = cpu_to_be32(sbi->s_sys_blocksize - sizeof(struct omfs_header));`, a crafted on-disk `s_sys_blocksize` smaller than the header/dir start would underflow the unsigned length used by `omfs_make_empty()`-style directory initialization and enable the out-of-bounds memset condition described. Because the needed minimum-size guard is absent here, the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet present.
